impact: The Agent server can be materialized/compiled in the source tree while the Core integrated installer still copies only the legacy ten-file payload into project_root/bridge. On a first integrated deployment this can publish server.py that imports local Agent modules which the transaction did not deploy or hash-bind. Runtime then depends on absent or stale modules outside the installer contract, so compile-only materialization is not an installation proof.
safety_boundary: This is an Agent <-> Core packaging/integration defect, not a new prompt/rotation/delegation algorithm and not the current NCM28 Windows/durable replay task.
required_fix: Define an explicit deployable local-module manifest/closure for the materialized Agent bridge.
Validate the closure before lifecycle stop or any managed source write.
Copy every required module under a runtime namespace consistent with its imports.
Include every deployed module in payload hashes, durable preimage backup, outer journal descriptors, installed marker, rollback and final verification.
Fail closed before mutation if an imported local module is outside the deployment manifest.
Add a regression that materializes the Agent pair and checks the deployed bridge import closure, not merely compile(server.py) in the source checkout.
